meaningEn: the simulation of human intelligence processes by computer systems
exampleEn: Artificial intelligence is transforming industries from healthcare to finance.
exampleCn: 人工智能正在改变从医疗到金融等各行各业。
confusableWords: artificial intelligence vs. machine learning: AI is the broad field; ML is a subset of AI focused on learning from data

meaningEn: a subset of AI where systems learn patterns from data to make predictions or decisions
exampleEn: Machine learning algorithms can detect fraud in real-time transactions.
exampleCn: 机器学习算法能够实时检测交易中的欺诈行为。
confusableWords: machine learning vs. deep learning: ML is the general field; DL is a subset using deep neural networks

meaningEn: a subset of ML using multi-layered neural networks to learn hierarchical representations
exampleEn: Deep learning has achieved breakthroughs in image and speech recognition.
exampleCn: 深度学习在图像和语音识别方面取得了突破。
synonyms: deep neural network learning, hierarchical feature learning
confusableWords: deep learning vs. machine learning: DL uses neural networks with many layers; ML encompasses broader techniques

meaningEn: a computing system inspired by biological neural networks, composed of interconnected nodes
exampleEn: The neural network was trained on millions of labeled images.
exampleCn: 该神经网络在数百万张标记图像上进行了训练。
synonyms: neural net, artificial neural network, ANN
confusableWords: neural network vs. neural net: synonymous; neural network is the formal term

meaningEn: a step-by-step procedure or set of rules for solving a problem or performing a computation
exampleEn: The sorting algorithm runs in O(n log n) time complexity.
exampleCn: 该排序算法的时间复杂度为 O(n log n)。
confusableWords: algorithm vs. heuristic: an algorithm is a defined procedure; a heuristic is a rule-of-thumb approach

meaningEn: a mathematical representation of a real-world process learned from training data
exampleEn: We evaluated three models on the test set and chose the best-performing one.
exampleCn: 我们在测试集上评估了三个模型，选择了性能最好的一个。
synonyms: predictive model, statistical model, learned model
confusableWords: model vs. algorithm: an algorithm is the method; a model is the learned output of applying that algorithm to data

meaningEn: the process of feeding data to an algorithm so it can learn patterns and adjust parameters
exampleEn: Training the model on GPU took approximately 12 hours.
exampleCn: 在GPU上训练模型大约花了12小时。
confusableWords: training vs. inference: training is learning; inference is applying the learned model to new data

meaningEn: the process of using a trained model to make predictions on new, unseen data
exampleEn: The inference pipeline processes each request in under 50 milliseconds.
exampleCn: 推理流水线处理每个请求不到50毫秒。
confusableWords: inference vs. training: inference applies a trained model; training creates the model

meaningEn: the output produced by a model when given new input data
exampleEn: The model's prediction accuracy on the validation set was 94.2%.
exampleCn: 模型在验证集上的预测准确率为94.2%。
confusableWords: prediction vs. inference: prediction is the result/output; inference is the process

meaningEn: a supervised learning task of assigning input data to predefined categories or labels
exampleEn: Email spam detection is a classic binary classification problem.
exampleCn: 邮件垃圾检测是一个经典的二分类问题。
confusableWords: classification vs. clustering: classification uses known labels; clustering discovers groups without labels

meaningEn: a supervised learning task of predicting a continuous numerical value from input features
exampleEn: Linear regression models the relationship between input variables and a continuous target.
exampleCn: 线性回归对输入变量与连续目标之间的关系进行建模。
confusableWords: regression (ML) vs. regression (statistics): in ML, it means predicting continuous values; in stats, it includes the same but also hypothesis testing

meaningEn: an unsupervised learning task of grouping similar data points together
exampleEn: K-means clustering grouped the customers into five distinct segments.
exampleCn: K均值聚类将客户分成五个不同的群体。
confusableWords: clustering vs. classification: clustering is unsupervised (no labels); classification is supervised (uses labels)

meaningEn: a learning paradigm where the model is trained on labeled input-output pairs
exampleEn: Supervised learning requires a dataset with both features and ground-truth labels.
exampleCn: 有监督学习需要一个包含特征和真实标签的数据集。
rootAffix: super- (above/over) + vis (see, from Latin videre) + -ed + learning
confusableWords: supervised vs. unsupervised learning: supervised uses labeled data; unsupervised discovers patterns without labels

meaningEn: a learning paradigm where the model finds hidden patterns in unlabeled data
exampleEn: Unsupervised learning revealed three latent topics in the document corpus.
exampleCn: 无监督学习在文档语料库中揭示了三个潜在主题。
confusableWords: unsupervised learning vs. self-supervised learning: unsupervised has no labels at all; self-supervised creates pseudo-labels from data itself

meaningEn: a learning paradigm where an agent learns by interacting with an environment to maximize cumulative reward
exampleEn: Reinforcement learning trained the agent to play Go at a superhuman level.
exampleCn: 强化学习训练了智能体以超人类水平下围棋。
confusableWords: reinforcement learning vs. supervised learning: RL learns from rewards/signals via interaction; SL learns from labeled examples

meaningEn: a technique where a model trained on one task is adapted for a different but related task
exampleEn: Transfer learning from ImageNet pretraining significantly boosted our accuracy on medical images.
exampleCn: 来自ImageNet预训练的迁移学习显著提升了我们在医学图像上的准确率。
confusableWords: transfer learning vs. fine-tuning: transfer learning is the general concept; fine-tuning is a specific method of transfer learning

meaningEn: an individual measurable property or characteristic of data used as input to a model
exampleEn: Feature engineering transformed raw timestamps into day-of-week and hour-of-day features.
exampleCn: 特征工程将原始时间戳转换成了星期几和小时这两个特征。
confusableWords: feature vs. label: features are inputs; labels are outputs the model tries to predict

meaningEn: the ground-truth output or category assigned to each training example
exampleEn: Each image in the dataset comes with a label indicating the object class.
exampleCn: 数据集中的每张图像都带有一个指示物体类别的标签。
confusableWords: label vs. annotation: in ML, they are often used interchangeably; annotation is the process of creating labels

meaningEn: a collection of data examples used for training, validation, or testing a model
exampleEn: The dataset was split into 80% training, 10% validation, and 10% test sets.
exampleCn: 数据集被划分为80%训练集、10%验证集和10%测试集。
confusableWords: dataset vs. database: a dataset is a static collection for analysis; a database is a managed, queryable system

meaningEn: when a model learns noise and details of training data to the extent that it performs poorly on new data
exampleEn: Regularization and dropout were added to prevent the model from overfitting.
exampleCn: 添加了正则化和dropout来防止模型过拟合。
confusableWords: overfitting vs. underfitting: overfitting = too complex, memorizes noise; underfitting = too simple, fails to capture patterns

meaningEn: when a model is too simple to capture the underlying patterns in the data
exampleEn: Increasing the model capacity helped resolve the underfitting issue.
exampleCn: 增加模型容量帮助解决了欠拟合问题。
confusableWords: underfitting vs. overfitting: underfitting fails to learn; overfitting learns too much including noise

meaningEn: an error introduced by approximating a complex problem with a simpler model; also systematic unfairness in data or predictions
exampleEn: High bias in the model indicates it may be underfitting the training data.
exampleCn: 模型中的高偏差表明它可能对训练数据欠拟合。
confusableWords: bias (ML) vs. bias (ethics): in ML, bias-variance tradeoff refers to error from simplification; in ethics, bias means unfair discrimination

meaningEn: the error introduced by a model's sensitivity to fluctuations in the training set
exampleEn: Reducing variance often requires more training data or regularization techniques.
exampleCn: 降低方差通常需要更多训练数据或正则化技术。
confusableWords: variance (ML) vs. variance (statistics): ML variance is model sensitivity; statistical variance measures spread of data

meaningEn: a technique to prevent overfitting by adding a penalty term to the loss function
exampleEn: L2 regularization penalizes large weights to keep the model simpler.
exampleCn: L2正则化通过惩罚大权重来保持模型的简洁性。
confusableWords: L1 regularization (lasso) vs. L2 regularization (ridge): L1 can produce zero weights (sparsity); L2 produces small but non-zero weights

meaningEn: the process of evaluating a model on a held-out dataset to tune hyperparameters and assess generalization
exampleEn: We used k-fold cross-validation to obtain a reliable estimate of model performance.
exampleCn: 我们使用了k折交叉验证来获得可靠的模型性能估计。
confusableWords: validation set vs. test set: validation set is for tuning; test set is for final, unbiased evaluation

meaningEn: the final evaluation of a trained model on unseen data to estimate real-world performance
exampleEn: The testing phase revealed that the model generalizes well to unseen images.
exampleCn: 测试阶段显示该模型对未见图像具有良好的泛化能力。
rootAffix: test (from Latin testum, vessel for testing) + -ing
confusableWords: testing vs. validation: validation is for tuning; testing is the final unbiased evaluation

meaningEn: a resampling technique where data is split into multiple folds to assess model stability
exampleEn: 5-fold cross-validation gave us confidence that the results were not a fluke.
exampleCn: 5折交叉验证让我们确信结果并非偶然。
confusableWords: cross-validation vs. holdout: cross-validation uses multiple splits; holdout uses a single static split

meaningEn: a configuration variable set before training that controls the learning process
exampleEn: Grid search was used to find the optimal hyperparameter values for the model.
exampleCn: 网格搜索被用来寻找模型的最优超参数值。
confusableWords: hyperparameter vs. parameter: hyperparameters are set before training (e.g., learning rate); parameters are learned during training (e.g., weights)

meaningEn: one complete pass through the entire training dataset during model training
exampleEn: The model converged after 50 epochs of training on the full dataset.
exampleCn: 模型在完整数据集上训练50个epoch后收敛。
rootAffix: from Greek epochē (pause, fixed point of time)
confusableWords: epoch vs. iteration: one epoch = one full pass through the dataset; one iteration = one batch update

meaningEn: the number of training examples processed in one forward/backward pass iteration
exampleEn: Increasing the batch size from 32 to 128 reduced training time per epoch.
exampleCn: 将批大小从32增加到128减少了每个epoch的训练时间。
rootAffix: batch (from Old French bache, bundle) + size
confusableWords: batch size vs. epoch: batch size is examples per step; epoch is full dataset passes

meaningEn: a hyperparameter that controls how much to update model weights in response to the estimated error
exampleEn: A learning rate that is too high can cause the loss to diverge instead of converge.
exampleCn: 学习率过高可能导致损失函数发散而非收敛。
confusableWords: learning rate vs. momentum: learning rate controls step magnitude; momentum controls direction smoothing

meaningEn: the vector of partial derivatives of the loss function with respect to each model parameter
exampleEn: Gradient descent updates weights in the direction opposite to the gradient.
exampleCn: 梯度下降沿着梯度的反方向更新权重。
confusableWords: gradient vs. derivative: gradient is the vector of all partial derivatives; derivative is a scalar for single-variable functions

meaningEn: a function that measures how well the model's predictions match the true labels
exampleEn: Cross-entropy loss function is commonly used for multi-class classification tasks.
exampleCn: 交叉熵损失函数通常用于多分类任务。
synonyms: cost function, objective function, error function
confusableWords: loss function vs. cost function: often used interchangeably; cost function may refer to the average loss over the whole dataset

meaningEn: an algorithm that adjusts model parameters to minimize the loss function
exampleEn: Adam optimizer combines momentum with adaptive learning rates for faster convergence.
exampleCn: Adam优化器结合了动量和自适应学习率，实现了更快的收敛。
confusableWords: SGD vs. Adam: SGD is simple gradient descent; Adam adds momentum and per-parameter adaptive rates

meaningEn: the state where continued training yields diminishing improvements in the loss function
exampleEn: The training loss stabilized after 200 iterations, indicating convergence.
exampleCn: 训练损失在200次迭代后趋于稳定，表明已收敛。
confusableWords: convergence vs. local minimum: convergence means loss stops changing; local minimum is a specific type of converged state

meaningEn: a model's ability to perform well on new, previously unseen data
exampleEn: Dropout improved the model's generalization on the held-out test set.
exampleCn: Dropout改善了模型在保留测试集上的泛化能力。
confusableWords: generalization vs. overfitting: good generalization = performs on new data; overfitting = only performs on training data

meaningEn: the proportion of correct predictions among all predictions made
exampleEn: The classifier achieved 97% accuracy on the balanced test dataset.
exampleCn: 分类器在平衡测试数据集上达到了97%的准确率。
confusableWords: accuracy vs. F1-score: accuracy is overall correctness; F1 balances precision and recall, better for imbalanced data

meaningEn: the proportion of true positive predictions among all positive predictions
exampleEn: High precision means the model produces very few false positive errors.
exampleCn: 高精确率意味着模型产生的假阳性错误非常少。
confusableWords: precision vs. recall: precision = how many predicted positives are correct; recall = how many actual positives were found

meaningEn: the proportion of true positive predictions among all actual positive examples
exampleEn: In medical diagnosis, high recall is critical to avoid missing patients with the disease.
exampleCn: 在医学诊断中，高召回率至关重要，以避免漏诊患病患者。
confusableWords: recall vs. precision: recall focuses on finding all positives; precision focuses on correctness of positive predictions

meaningEn: the harmonic mean of precision and recall, providing a balanced measure of classification performance
exampleEn: The F1-score of 0.89 indicates a good balance between precision and recall.
exampleCn: 0.89的F1分数表明精确率和召回率之间取得了良好平衡。
confusableWords: F1-score vs. accuracy: F1 balances precision/recall; accuracy can be misleading on imbalanced datasets

meaningEn: the basic computational unit in a neural network that receives inputs, applies weights and an activation, and produces an output
exampleEn: Each neuron in the hidden layer computes a weighted sum followed by a nonlinear activation.
exampleCn: 隐藏层中的每个神经元计算加权和，然后应用非线性激活函数。
confusableWords: neuron (biological) vs. neuron (ANN): biological neurons are brain cells; ANN neurons are mathematical functions inspired by them

meaningEn: the simplest type of neural network with a single layer of weights and a step activation function
exampleEn: The perceptron can only solve linearly separable classification problems.
exampleCn: 感知机只能解决线性可分的分类问题。
confusableWords: perceptron vs. multilayer perceptron: perceptron has no hidden layers; MLP has one or more hidden layers

meaningEn: a layer of neurons between the input and output layers in a neural network
exampleEn: Adding more hidden layers enables the network to learn more complex features.
exampleCn: 添加更多隐藏层使网络能够学习更复杂的特征。
confusableWords: hidden layer vs. input layer: hidden layers transform representations; input layers pass through raw features

meaningEn: a nonlinear function applied to a neuron's output to introduce nonlinearity into the network
exampleEn: ReLU is the most commonly used activation function in deep neural networks.
exampleCn: ReLU是深度神经网络中最常用的激活函数。
confusableWords: ReLU vs. sigmoid: ReLU avoids vanishing gradient; sigmoid squashes output to (0,1) but can cause vanishing gradients

meaningEn: Rectified Linear Unit, an activation function that outputs the input directly if positive, otherwise zero
exampleEn: ReLU activation function is defined as f(x) = max(0, x).
exampleCn: ReLU激活函数定义为 f(x) = max(0, x)。
confusableWords: ReLU vs. Leaky ReLU: standard ReLU outputs 0 for negative inputs; Leaky ReLU allows a small gradient for negatives

meaningEn: an S-shaped activation function that maps any real-valued number to the range (0, 1)
exampleEn: The sigmoid function is often used in the output layer for binary classification.
exampleCn: sigmoid函数常用于二分类的输出层。
confusableWords: sigmoid vs. softmax: sigmoid is for binary classification; softmax generalizes to multi-class

meaningEn: an activation function that converts a vector of raw scores into a probability distribution
exampleEn: The softmax function ensures the output probabilities sum to one for each class.
exampleCn: softmax函数确保每个类别的输出概率之和为一。
confusableWords: softmax vs. sigmoid: softmax is for multi-class (K > 2); sigmoid is for binary (K = 2)

meaningEn: a mathematical operation that slides a kernel across input data to produce feature maps
exampleEn: The convolution operation extracts local patterns such as edges and textures from images.
exampleCn: 卷积操作从图像中提取边缘和纹理等局部模式。
confusableWords: convolution (math) vs. convolution (CNN): mathematically the same operation; in CNNs, convolution is cross-correlation (no kernel flip)

meaningEn: a downsampling operation that reduces the spatial dimensions of feature maps
exampleEn: Max pooling selects the maximum value in each pooling window to retain prominent features.
exampleCn: 最大池化选择每个池化窗口中的最大值以保留显著特征。
confusableWords: max pooling vs. average pooling: max pooling takes the maximum; average pooling takes the mean

meaningEn: Convolutional Neural Network, a deep learning architecture designed for processing grid-like data such as images
exampleEn: CNNs achieved human-level performance on the ImageNet classification benchmark.
exampleCn: 卷积神经网络在ImageNet分类基准上达到了人类水平的性能。
confusableWords: CNN vs. ResNet: CNN is the general architecture; ResNet is a specific CNN variant with residual connections

meaningEn: Recurrent Neural Network, a neural network architecture designed for sequential data by maintaining hidden state across time steps
exampleEn: RNNs can process variable-length text sequences for tasks like sentiment analysis.
exampleCn: 循环神经网络可以处理变长文本序列，用于情感分析等任务。
confusableWords: RNN vs. LSTM: RNN suffers from vanishing gradients on long sequences; LSTM solves this with gating mechanisms

meaningEn: Long Short-Term Memory, an RNN variant with gating mechanisms to capture long-range dependencies
exampleEn: LSTM networks outperform standard RNNs on tasks requiring long-term memory.
exampleCn: 在需要长期记忆的任务上，LSTM网络优于标准RNN。
confusableWords: LSTM vs. GRU: both solve vanishing gradients; LSTM has 3 gates (input, forget, output); GRU has 2 gates (reset, update) and is simpler

meaningEn: Gated Recurrent Unit, a simplified LSTM variant with reset and update gates for sequential modeling
exampleEn: GRU achieves comparable performance to LSTM with fewer parameters and faster training.
exampleCn: GRU以更少的参数和更快的训练速度，达到了与LSTM相当的性能。
confusableWords: GRU vs. LSTM: GRU has fewer gates, faster; LSTM is more expressive, better for complex dependencies

meaningEn: a technique that allows a model to focus on the most relevant parts of the input when producing output
exampleEn: The attention mechanism enables the model to focus on specific words when generating translations.
exampleCn: 注意力机制使模型在生成翻译时能够关注特定的词语。
rootAffix: attend (stretch toward, from Latin attendere) + -tion + mechanism
confusableWords: self-attention vs. cross-attention: self-attention relates positions within the same sequence; cross-attention relates positions across two sequences

meaningEn: a neural network architecture based on self-attention mechanisms, widely used in NLP and beyond
exampleEn: The transformer architecture revolutionized natural language processing with the introduction of BERT and GPT.
exampleCn: Transformer架构通过BERT和GPT的引入彻底改变了自然语言处理。
confusableWords: transformer vs. attention mechanism: transformer is an architecture; attention is a key component within it

meaningEn: a component that converts input data into a compressed internal representation
exampleEn: The encoder processes the input sentence and produces a context-aware representation.
exampleCn: 编码器处理输入句子并生成上下文感知的表示。
confusableWords: encoder vs. decoder: encoder compresses input into representation; decoder generates output from that representation

meaningEn: a component that generates output from an internal representation produced by an encoder
exampleEn: The decoder generates the output translation token by token from the encoded representation.
exampleCn: 解码器从编码表示中逐个令牌生成输出翻译。
confusableWords: decoder-only vs. encoder-decoder: decoder-only (GPT) generates text; encoder-decoder (T5) both encodes and decodes

meaningEn: sequence-to-sequence, a model architecture that maps an input sequence to an output sequence
exampleEn: Seq2seq models are widely used for machine translation and text summarization.
exampleCn: 序列到序列模型广泛应用于机器翻译和文本摘要。
confusableWords: seq2seq vs. transformer: seq2seq is a paradigm; transformer is one architecture for implementing seq2seq

meaningEn: a dense vector representation of discrete items such as words or tokens in a continuous vector space
exampleEn: Word embeddings capture semantic relationships, such as king minus man plus woman equals queen.
exampleCn: 词嵌入捕获语义关系，例如king减去man加上woman等于queen。
synonyms: dense representation, vector embedding, distributed representation
confusableWords: embedding vs. encoding: embedding produces dense vectors; encoding (one-hot) produces sparse vectors

meaningEn: the process of splitting text into individual tokens (words, subwords, or characters)
exampleEn: Tokenization splits the sentence into units that the model can process.
exampleCn: 分词将句子拆分为模型可以处理的单元。
confusableWords: tokenization vs. stemming: tokenization splits text into pieces; stemming reduces words to root form (e.g., running → run)

meaningEn: Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers, a pre-trained language model using masked language modeling
exampleEn: BERT achieved state-of-the-art results on numerous NLP benchmark tasks.
exampleCn: BERT在众多NLP基准任务上取得了最先进的结果。
rootAffix: acronym: Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers
confusableWords: BERT vs. GPT: BERT is bidirectional encoder (understanding); GPT is autoregressive decoder (generation)

meaningEn: Generative Pre-trained Transformer, a large language model that generates text autoregressively
exampleEn: GPT-4 demonstrates remarkable capabilities in reasoning, coding, and creative writing.
exampleCn: GPT-4在推理、编程和创意写作方面展现了卓越的能力。
confusableWords: GPT vs. BERT: GPT generates text left-to-right; BERT encodes text bidirectionally for understanding tasks

meaningEn: a model that assigns probabilities to sequences of words or tokens
exampleEn: A language model can predict the next word in a sentence given the preceding context.
exampleCn: 语言模型可以根据前面的上下文预测句子中的下一个词。
synonyms: LM, statistical language model, neural language model
confusableWords: language model vs. large language model: LM is general; LLM specifically refers to very large-scale models

meaningEn: a pre-training objective where random tokens are masked and the model must predict them from context
exampleEn: BERT uses a masked language model objective during pre-training.
exampleCn: BERT在预训练阶段使用掩码语言模型目标。
confusableWords: MLM vs. CLM: MLM masks random tokens bidirectionally (BERT); CLM predicts next token left-to-right (GPT)

meaningEn: a pre-training objective where the model predicts the next token given only preceding tokens
exampleEn: GPT uses a causal language model objective, predicting each token based on previous ones.
exampleCn: GPT使用因果语言模型目标，基于前面的令牌预测每个令牌。
rootAffix: causal (from Latin causa, cause) + language model
confusableWords: causal LM vs. masked LM: causal LM predicts next token; masked LM fills in blanks bidirectionally

meaningEn: a property of a model that generates output one step at a time, conditioning on its own previous outputs
exampleEn: Autoregressive models generate text by sampling each token conditioned on previously generated tokens.
exampleCn: 自回归模型通过在先前生成的令牌条件下采样每个令牌来生成文本。
confusableWords: autoregressive vs. non-autoregressive: autoregressive generates one token at a time; non-autoregressive generates all tokens in parallel

meaningEn: processing information in both forward and backward directions simultaneously
exampleEn: BERT's bidirectional encoder can leverage both left and right context to understand each word.
exampleCn: BERT的双向编码器可以同时利用左右上下文来理解每个词。
confusableWords: bidirectional (BERT) vs. unidirectional (GPT): bidirectional sees full context; unidirectional only sees preceding tokens

meaningEn: the process of further training a pre-trained model on a specific downstream task with a smaller dataset
exampleEn: Fine-tuning BERT on our domain-specific data improved classification accuracy by 15%.
exampleCn: 在我们领域特定数据上微调BERT使分类准确率提高了15%。
confusableWords: fine-tuning vs. pre-training: pre-training learns general features on large data; fine-tuning adapts to specific tasks

meaningEn: the initial phase of training a model on a large, general dataset before adapting it to specific tasks
exampleEn: Pretraining on billions of tokens provides the model with broad linguistic knowledge.
exampleCn: 在数十亿个令牌上进行预训练为模型提供了广泛的语言知识。
confusableWords: pretraining vs. fine-tuning: pretraining = general learning on big data; fine-tuning = task-specific adaptation

meaningEn: a large model trained on broad data that can be adapted to a wide range of downstream tasks
exampleEn: Foundation models serve as a base for many specialized applications through fine-tuning or prompting.
exampleCn: 基础模型通过微调或提示成为许多专门应用的基础。
confusableWords: foundation model vs. LLM: foundation model is broader (includes vision, multimodal); LLM specifically refers to language foundation models

meaningEn: a foundation model with billions of parameters trained on massive text corpora for language understanding and generation
exampleEn: Large language models like GPT-4 and Claude demonstrate emergent capabilities at scale.
exampleCn: 像GPT-4和Claude这样的大语言模型在规模上展现了涌现能力。
confusableWords: LLM vs. foundation model: LLM is a language-specific foundation model; foundation model includes vision and multimodal models

meaningEn: abbreviation for Large Language Model
exampleEn: The rapid adoption of LLMs has transformed software development workflows.
exampleCn: LLM的快速采用改变了软件开发工作流程。
synonyms: large language model, foundation language model
confusableWords: LLM vs. LLMs: singular LLM refers to the class; plural LLMs refers to specific models

meaningEn: the practice of designing and optimizing input prompts to guide language model outputs
exampleEn: Prompt engineering techniques like chain-of-thought significantly improve reasoning performance.
exampleCn: 像思维链这样的提示工程技术显著提升了推理性能。
confusableWords: prompt engineering vs. fine-tuning: prompt engineering guides output via text input; fine-tuning modifies model weights

meaningEn: a prompting technique that encourages models to generate intermediate reasoning steps before producing a final answer
exampleEn: Chain-of-thought prompting helps large language models solve complex math and logic problems.
exampleCn: 思维链提示帮助大语言模型解决复杂的数学和逻辑问题。
confusableWords: chain-of-thought vs. few-shot: CoT focuses on reasoning steps; few-shot provides example inputs/outputs

meaningEn: a learning paradigm where a model learns a new task from only a few labeled examples
exampleEn: With few-shot learning, GPT can perform text classification with just 5 examples.
exampleCn: 通过少样本学习，GPT仅需5个示例就能完成文本分类。
confusableWords: few-shot vs. zero-shot: few-shot provides a few examples in the prompt; zero-shot provides no examples

meaningEn: the ability of a model to perform a task it was not explicitly trained on, without any task-specific examples
exampleEn: Zero-shot learning enables the model to translate between languages it was not specifically trained on.
exampleCn: 零样本学习使模型能够在未经专门训练的语言之间进行翻译。
confusableWords: zero-shot vs. few-shot: zero-shot uses no task examples; few-shot uses a small number of task examples

meaningEn: the ability of large language models to learn new tasks from examples provided within the prompt context
exampleEn: In-context learning allows language models to adapt to new tasks without updating their weights.
exampleCn: 上下文学习允许语言模型在不更新权重的情况下适应新任务。
confusableWords: in-context learning vs. fine-tuning: in-context learning uses prompt examples only; fine-tuning updates model parameters

meaningEn: Retrieval-Augmented Generation, a technique combining information retrieval with language model generation
exampleEn: RAG systems retrieve relevant documents from a knowledge base to ground the model's responses.
exampleCn: RAG系统从知识库中检索相关文档，以支撑模型的回答。
confusableWords: RAG vs. fine-tuning: RAG retrieves external knowledge at inference time; fine-tuning bakes knowledge into weights

meaningEn: when a language model generates content that is incorrect, fabricated, or not supported by the input or real-world facts
meaningCn: n. 幻觉（模型生成虚假内容）
exampleEn: Hallucination remains a major challenge for deploying language models in high-stakes domains like medicine.
exampleCn: 幻觉问题仍是在医疗等高风险领域部署语言模型的主要挑战。
rootAffix: from Latin hallucinari (to wander in mind) + -tion
confusableWords: hallucination vs. error: hallucination specifically means plausible-sounding but false content; error can be any mistake

meaningEn: the task of assigning a category label to an entire image
exampleEn: Image classification models can distinguish between cats and dogs with over 99% accuracy.
exampleCn: 图像分类模型能以超过99%的准确率区分猫和狗。
confusableWords: image classification vs. object detection: classification labels the whole image; detection finds and labels individual objects within it

meaningEn: the task of locating and classifying multiple objects within an image using bounding boxes
exampleEn: Object detection is used in autonomous vehicles to identify pedestrians and other cars.
exampleCn: 目标检测用于自动驾驶汽车以识别行人和其他车辆。
confusableWords: object detection vs. image segmentation: detection draws bounding boxes; segmentation creates pixel-level masks

meaningEn: the task of assigning a class label to every pixel in an image, grouping pixels into semantic categories
exampleEn: Semantic segmentation distinguishes road, sidewalk, buildings, and sky in street-view images.
exampleCn: 语义分割在街景图像中区分道路、人行道、建筑物和天空。
confusableWords: semantic vs. instance segmentation: semantic groups same-class pixels together; instance separates individual objects

meaningEn: the task of detecting and delineating each individual object instance at the pixel level
exampleEn: Instance segmentation differentiates between each person in a crowded scene.
exampleCn: 实例分割能够区分拥挤场景中的每一个人。
confusableWords: instance vs. semantic segmentation: instance distinguishes individual objects; semantic only distinguishes categories

meaningEn: You Only Look Once, a real-time object detection algorithm that predicts bounding boxes and class probabilities in a single pass
exampleEn: YOLO can process video frames at over 60 FPS for real-time object detection.
exampleCn: YOLO能以超过60FPS的速度处理视频帧，实现实时目标检测。
confusableWords: YOLO vs. R-CNN: YOLO is single-stage (fast); R-CNN is two-stage (more accurate but slower)

meaningEn: a rectangular box that defines the location and extent of an object within an image
exampleEn: The bounding box coordinates are defined by x, y, width, and height values.
exampleCn: 边界框坐标由x、y、宽度和高度值定义。
confusableWords: bounding box vs. segmentation mask: bounding box is a rectangle; segmentation mask is pixel-accurate outline

meaningEn: the task of identifying or verifying a person's identity from a facial image
exampleEn: Face recognition technology is used for secure authentication in smartphones.
exampleCn: 人脸识别技术用于智能手机的安全认证。
confusableWords: face recognition vs. face detection: detection finds faces in images; recognition identifies whose face it is

meaningEn: Optical Character Recognition, the conversion of images of text into machine-readable text
exampleEn: OCR technology digitizes scanned documents by extracting printed or handwritten text.
exampleCn: OCR技术通过提取印刷或手写文本将扫描文档数字化。
confusableWords: OCR vs. ICR: OCR handles printed text; ICR (Intelligent Character Recognition) handles handwriting

meaningEn: the task of creating new images from text descriptions, noise, or other inputs using generative models
exampleEn: Diffusion models have achieved remarkable quality in image generation from text prompts.
exampleCn: 扩散模型在从文本提示生成图像方面取得了惊人的质量。
confusableWords: image generation vs. image enhancement: generation creates new images; enhancement improves existing ones

meaningEn: a generative model that creates images by gradually denoising a random noise signal
exampleEn: Stable Diffusion is a widely-used diffusion model for text-to-image generation.
exampleCn: Stable Diffusion是广泛使用的文本到图像生成扩散模型。
confusableWords: diffusion model vs. GAN: diffusion models iteratively denoise; GANs use adversarial training. Diffusion models generally produce higher quality

meaningEn: Generative Adversarial Network, a model with a generator and discriminator trained competitively
exampleEn: GANs can generate photorealistic faces that are indistinguishable from real photographs.
exampleCn: GAN能够生成与真实照片难以区分的逼真人脸。
confusableWords: GAN vs. VAE: GAN uses adversarial training; VAE uses variational inference. GANs produce sharper images; VAEs are more stable to train

meaningEn: Variational Autoencoder, a generative model that learns a probabilistic latent space from data
exampleEn: VAEs can generate new data samples by sampling from the learned latent distribution.
exampleCn: VAE可以通过从学习的潜分布中采样来生成新的数据样本。
confusableWords: VAE vs. autoencoder: VAE learns a probability distribution in latent space; standard autoencoder learns deterministic mapping

meaningEn: a neural network that learns to compress data into a latent representation and reconstruct it
exampleEn: Autoencoders are used for dimensionality reduction and anomaly detection.
exampleCn: 自编码器用于降维和异常检测。
confusableWords: autoencoder vs. VAE: autoencoder uses deterministic encoding; VAE uses probabilistic encoding with a loss that includes KL divergence

meaningEn: increasing the spatial resolution of feature maps or images
exampleEn: Upsampling layers in the decoder restore the spatial resolution of the feature maps.
exampleCn: 解码器中的上采样层恢复特征图的空间分辨率。
confusableWords: upsampling vs. transposed convolution: upsampling is interpolation; transposed convolution is a learnable upsampling operation

meaningEn: reducing the spatial resolution or the number of samples in data
exampleEn: Downsampling the image from 4K to 1080p reduces computation cost significantly.
exampleCn: 将图像从4K下采样到1080p显著降低了计算成本。
confusableWords: downsampling vs. pooling: downsampling is the general concept; pooling is a specific downsampling technique in CNNs

meaningEn: the process of identifying and representing important patterns or structures from raw data
exampleEn: CNN layers perform hierarchical feature extraction from low-level edges to high-level shapes.
exampleCn: CNN层执行从低级边缘到高级形状的层次化特征提取。
rootAffix: feature + ex- (out) + tract (pull, from Latin trahere) + -ion
confusableWords: feature extraction vs. feature engineering: extraction learns features automatically; engineering manually creates them

meaningEn: a neural network layer that performs convolution operations on its input using learnable filters
exampleEn: The first convolutional layer detects simple features like edges and corners.
exampleCn: 第一个卷积层检测边缘和角点等简单特征。
confusableWords: convolutional layer vs. fully connected layer: conv layers preserve spatial structure; FC layers flatten and connect all neurons

meaningEn: a layer that performs downsampling on feature maps to reduce spatial dimensions
exampleEn: A pooling layer with 2x2 window size halves the spatial dimensions of the feature map.
exampleCn: 使用2×2窗口大小的池化层将特征图的空间尺寸减半。
confusableWords: pooling layer vs. strided convolution: pooling uses fixed operations (max/avg); strided convolution uses learnable filters with stride > 1

meaningEn: a technique that normalizes layer inputs across each mini-batch to stabilize and accelerate training
exampleEn: Batch normalization enables higher learning rates and reduces sensitivity to weight initialization.
exampleCn: 批归一化允许更高的学习率并减少对权重初始化的敏感性。
confusableWords: batch normalization vs. layer normalization: BN normalizes across batch dimension; LN normalizes across feature dimension per sample

meaningEn: a skip connection that adds the input of a layer directly to its output, helping with gradient flow in deep networks
exampleEn: Residual connections in ResNet allow training of networks with over 100 layers.
exampleCn: ResNet中的残差连接允许训练超过100层的网络。
confusableWords: residual connection vs. dense connection: residual adds input to output; dense connection (DenseNet) concatenates all previous outputs

meaningEn: the task of predicting the distance of each pixel from the camera in an image
exampleEn: Monocular depth estimation predicts depth from a single image without stereo cameras.
exampleCn: 单目深度估计无需立体相机即可从单张图像预测深度。
confusableWords: depth estimation vs. disparity estimation: depth is actual distance; disparity is pixel difference in stereo pairs

meaningEn: the task of detecting the position and orientation of human body joints or objects in images
exampleEn: Pose estimation is used in fitness apps to track exercise form in real-time.
exampleCn: 姿态估计用于健身应用中实时追踪运动姿势。
confusableWords: pose estimation vs. pose recognition: estimation finds keypoint positions; recognition classifies the pose category

meaningEn: the pattern of apparent motion of objects between consecutive video frames
exampleEn: Optical flow algorithms estimate pixel-wise motion vectors between video frames.
exampleCn: 光流算法估计视频帧之间的逐像素运动向量。
confusableWords: optical flow vs. motion detection: optical flow provides dense pixel-level motion; motion detection is binary (moved or not)

meaningEn: a set of 3D data points representing the external surface of objects captured by depth sensors or LiDAR
exampleEn: LiDAR sensors generate point clouds used for 3D scene understanding in autonomous driving.
exampleCn: 激光雷达传感器生成用于自动驾驶中3D场景理解的点云。
confusableWords: point cloud vs. mesh: point cloud is unstructured points; mesh is connected polygons forming surfaces

meaningEn: the process of building a 3D model of a scene or object from multiple 2D images or depth data
exampleEn: Multi-view 3D reconstruction creates detailed 3D models from photographs taken at different angles.
exampleCn: 多视角三维重建从不同角度拍摄的照片创建详细的3D模型。
confusableWords: 3D reconstruction vs. depth estimation: reconstruction builds full 3D geometry; estimation predicts per-pixel distances

meaningEn: the process of improving the visual quality of an image, such as contrast, brightness, or sharpness
exampleEn: Image enhancement algorithms improve low-light photographs for better visibility.
exampleCn: 图像增强算法改善低光照照片以获得更好的可见性。
confusableWords: image enhancement vs. image restoration: enhancement improves visual quality subjectively; restoration recovers the original signal objectively

meaningEn: the task of reconstructing a high-resolution image from a low-resolution input
exampleEn: Super-resolution models can enhance blurry surveillance footage to reveal fine details.
exampleCn: 超分辨率模型可以增强模糊的监控画面以揭示细节。
confusableWords: super-resolution vs. interpolation: super-resolution uses deep learning to hallucinate details; interpolation uses mathematical formulas

meaningEn: the technique of applying the artistic style of one image to the content of another
exampleEn: Neural style transfer can transform a photograph into a painting in the style of Van Gogh.
exampleCn: 神经风格迁移可以将照片转换成梵高风格的画作。
synonyms: artistic style transfer, neural style transfer
confusableWords: style transfer vs. image-to-image: style transfer specifically focuses on artistic style; image-to-image is a broader task

meaningEn: the task of filling in missing or corrupted regions of an image with plausible content
exampleEn: Inpainting can remove unwanted objects from photos by filling the area with coherent background.
exampleCn: 图像修复可以通过用一致的背景填充区域来移除照片中不需要的物体。
confusableWords: inpainting vs. outpainting: inpainting fills missing areas inside; outpainting extends the image beyond its borders

meaningEn: the task of translating an input image into a corresponding output image using a learned mapping
exampleEn: Image-to-image models can convert sketches to photorealistic images or day scenes to night scenes.
exampleCn: 图像到图像模型可以将草图转换为逼真图像或将白天场景转换为夜晚场景。
confusableWords: image-to-image vs. image generation: image-to-image takes an image as input; generation creates from scratch (e.g., from text)

meaningEn: a field of AI focused on enabling computers to understand, interpret, and generate human language
exampleEn: Natural language processing powers chatbots, search engines, and translation services.
exampleCn: 自然语言处理驱动了聊天机器人、搜索引擎和翻译服务。
confusableWords: NLP vs. NLU: NLP is the broad field; NLU is specifically about understanding meaning

meaningEn: Natural Language Understanding, the subfield of NLP focused on comprehending meaning from text or speech
exampleEn: NLU systems extract intent and entities from user utterances in conversational AI.
exampleCn: NLU系统从对话式AI中用户的话语中提取意图和实体。
confusableWords: NLU vs. NLG: NLU understands meaning (reading); NLG produces language (writing)

meaningEn: Natural Language Generation, the subfield of NLP focused on producing human-readable text from structured data or internal representations
exampleEn: NLG systems can summarize data reports in natural language for business users.
exampleCn: NLG系统可以用自然语言为业务用户总结数据报告。
confusableWords: NLG vs. NLU: NLG produces text; NLU understands and analyzes text

meaningEn: the task of identifying and classifying named entities such as people, organizations, and locations in text
exampleEn: Named entity recognition identified 'Apple' as an organization and 'Tim Cook' as a person in the article.
exampleCn: 命名实体识别在文章中将'Apple'识别为组织，将'Tim Cook'识别为人。
confusableWords: NER vs. NEL: NER finds and classifies entities; NEL (Named Entity Linking) connects them to a knowledge base

meaningEn: Part-of-Speech tagging, the task of assigning grammatical categories (noun, verb, etc.) to each word in a sentence
exampleEn: POS tagging identifies 'run' as a verb in 'She runs fast' and as a noun in 'Morning run'.
exampleCn: 词性标注将'She runs fast'中的'run'识别为动词，将'Morning run'中的识别为名词。
confusableWords: POS tagging vs. NER: POS assigns word categories (noun, verb); NER finds entity types (person, org)

meaningEn: the analysis of grammatical structure by identifying dependency relationships between words in a sentence
exampleEn: Dependency parsing reveals that 'quickly' modifies 'runs' in the sentence 'She runs quickly'.
exampleCn: 依存句法分析揭示了在句子'She runs quickly'中，'quickly'修饰'runs'。
rootAffix: depend (hang from) + -ency + parsing (from Latin pars, part)
confusableWords: dependency parsing vs. constituency parsing: dependency parsing shows word-to-word relations; constituency parsing shows hierarchical phrase structure

meaningEn: the task of determining the emotional tone (positive, negative, or neutral) of a text
exampleEn: Sentiment analysis of customer reviews helps businesses understand user satisfaction levels.
exampleCn: 对客户评论的情感分析帮助企业了解用户满意度。
confusableWords: sentiment analysis vs. emotion detection: sentiment is positive/negative/neutral; emotion detection identifies specific emotions (joy, anger, fear)

meaningEn: the task of assigning predefined categories to text documents
exampleEn: Text classification is used to route customer support emails to the appropriate department.
exampleCn: 文本分类用于将客户支持邮件路由到合适的部门。
confusableWords: text classification vs. text clustering: classification uses predefined categories; clustering discovers groups without labels

meaningEn: the task of automatically generating answers to natural language questions
exampleEn: Question answering systems power intelligent assistants like Siri and Alexa.
exampleCn: 问答系统驱动了Siri和Alexa等智能助手。
confusableWords: extractive QA vs. generative QA: extractive QA copies answer spans from text; generative QA produces free-form answers

meaningEn: the task of automatically translating text from one language to another
exampleEn: Neural machine translation has largely replaced rule-based systems for most language pairs.
exampleCn: 神经机器翻译已在大多数语言对中基本取代了基于规则的系统。
confusableWords: NMT vs. statistical MT: NMT uses neural networks end-to-end; statistical MT uses phrase-based models

meaningEn: the task of producing a concise summary that captures the key information of a longer document
exampleEn: Abstractive summarization generates new sentences that capture the main ideas of the article.
exampleCn: 抽象式摘要生成捕捉文章主要思想的新句子。
confusableWords: extractive vs. abstractive summarization: extractive copies important sentences; abstractive generates new text

meaningEn: the task of producing coherent and contextually appropriate text, often using language models
exampleEn: Large language models have dramatically improved the quality of text generation for various applications.
exampleCn: 大语言模型显著提升了各种应用中文本生成的质量。
confusableWords: text generation vs. text completion: generation produces full text; completion fills in the remaining part of a prefix

meaningEn: a decoding algorithm that explores multiple candidate sequences and selects the most probable one
exampleEn: Beam search with beam width 5 balances quality and speed during text generation.
exampleCn: 束宽度为5的束搜索在文本生成过程中平衡了质量和速度。
confusableWords: beam search vs. greedy search: beam search considers multiple candidates; greedy search picks the single best at each step

meaningEn: Bilingual Evaluation Understudy, a metric for evaluating the quality of machine-translated text against reference translations
exampleEn: The translation system achieved a BLEU score of 38.5 on the WMT benchmark.
exampleCn: 翻译系统在WMT基准上达到了38.5的BLEU分数。
confusableWords: BLEU vs. ROUGE: BLEU evaluates precision of n-grams (used for translation); ROUGE evaluates recall (used for summarization)

meaningEn: Recall-Oriented Understudy for Gisting Evaluation, a metric for evaluating text summarization quality
exampleEn: ROUGE-L scores measure the longest common subsequence between generated and reference summaries.
exampleCn: ROUGE-L分数衡量生成摘要和参考摘要之间的最长公共子序列。
rootAffix: acronym: Recall-Oriented Understudy for Gisting Evaluation
confusableWords: ROUGE vs. BLEU: ROUGE emphasizes recall (summarization); BLEU emphasizes precision (translation)

meaningEn: a discrete unit of text (word, subword, or character) used as input to language models
exampleEn: The BERT tokenizer splits 'unhappiness' into three tokens: 'un', 'hap', and 'piness'.
exampleCn: BERT分词器将'unhappiness'拆分为三个令牌：'un'、'hap'和'piness'。
confusableWords: token vs. word: a word is a natural language unit; a token is the processing unit, which may be a subword or character

meaningEn: the set of all unique tokens that a model can recognize and process
exampleEn: The model's vocabulary size of 50,000 tokens covers most common English words and subwords.
exampleCn: 模型的50,000个令牌词汇表覆盖了大多数常见的英语单词和子词。
confusableWords: vocabulary size vs. context length: vocabulary is the number of unique tokens known; context length is how many tokens can be processed at once

meaningEn: a unit of text smaller than a full word, used in tokenization strategies like BPE
exampleEn: Subword tokenization handles rare words by splitting them into frequent subword units.
exampleCn: 子词分词通过将罕见词拆分为频繁的子词单元来处理这些词。
confusableWords: subword vs. word: subword is part of a word (e.g., 'un-', '-ing'); word is a complete lexical unit

meaningEn: Byte Pair Encoding, a data compression algorithm adapted for subword tokenization in NLP
exampleEn: GPT models use BPE tokenization to handle open-vocabulary text efficiently.
exampleCn: GPT模型使用BPE分词来高效处理开放词汇表文本。
confusableWords: BPE vs. WordPiece: BPE merges most frequent byte pairs; WordPiece merges based on maximizing language model likelihood

meaningEn: a subword tokenization algorithm similar to BPE, used by BERT, that maximizes the likelihood of the training data
exampleEn: BERT uses WordPiece tokenization with a 30,000 token vocabulary.
exampleCn: BERT使用具有30,000令牌词汇表的WordPiece分词。
confusableWords: WordPiece vs. BPE: both merge subword units; WordPiece selects merges that maximize LM likelihood; BPE selects most frequent pairs

meaningEn: the task of assigning labels to each element in a sequence, such as POS tagging or NER
exampleEn: Sequence labeling models use BIO tags to identify entity boundaries in text.
exampleCn: 序列标注模型使用BIO标签来识别文本中的实体边界。
confusableWords: sequence labeling vs. sequence classification: labeling assigns a tag to each element; classification assigns a single label to the whole sequence

meaningEn: the task of identifying and classifying semantic relationships between entities in text
exampleEn: Relation extraction identifies that 'Steve Jobs' founded 'Apple' in the given sentence.
exampleCn: 关系抽取识别出在给定句子中'Steve Jobs'创立了'Apple'。
confusableWords: relation extraction vs. NER: NER finds entities; relation extraction finds relationships between entities

meaningEn: the task of determining which words in a text refer to the same entity
exampleEn: Coreference resolution determines that 'he' refers to 'Barack Obama' in the passage.
exampleCn: 共指消解确定段落中的'he'指的是'Barack Obama'。
confusableWords: coreference resolution vs. entity linking: coreference links mentions within a document; entity linking connects mentions to a knowledge base

meaningEn: the task of converting written text into natural-sounding spoken audio
exampleEn: Modern text-to-speech systems produce voices that are nearly indistinguishable from human speech.
exampleCn: 现代文本转语音系统产生的声音几乎与人类语音难以区分。
confusableWords: TTS vs. speech recognition: TTS converts text to audio; speech recognition converts audio to text

meaningEn: the task of converting spoken language into text or commands
exampleEn: Speech recognition enables voice assistants to understand and respond to user commands.
exampleCn: 语音识别使语音助手能够理解和回应用户命令。
confusableWords: speech recognition vs. speaker recognition: speech recognition converts audio to text; speaker recognition identifies who is speaking

meaningEn: a system that converses with humans using natural language, either task-oriented or open-domain
exampleEn: Dialog systems range from simple rule-based chatbots to sophisticated AI assistants powered by LLMs.
exampleCn: 对话系统从简单的基于规则的聊天机器人到由LLM驱动的复杂AI助手不等。
confusableWords: task-oriented vs. open-domain dialog: task-oriented (e.g., booking) has a defined goal; open-domain (e.g., chat) is free-form

meaningEn: a structured representation of entities and their relationships, stored as a graph of nodes and edges
exampleEn: Google's knowledge graph provides direct answers to factual questions in search results.
exampleCn: 谷歌的知识图谱在搜索结果中直接提供事实性问题的答案。
confusableWords: knowledge graph vs. database: knowledge graph focuses on entities and relationships; database is general-purpose data storage

meaningEn: the task of finding relevant documents or passages from a large collection in response to a query
exampleEn: Information retrieval systems power search engines by ranking documents by relevance to a user query.
exampleCn: 信息检索系统通过按与用户查询的相关性对文档排序来驱动搜索引擎。
rootAffix: information + re- (back) + trieve (find, from French trouver) + -al
confusableWords: information retrieval vs. knowledge extraction: retrieval finds existing documents; extraction discovers new knowledge from documents

meaningEn: the process of discovering patterns, trends, and knowledge from large volumes of unstructured text data
exampleEn: Text mining of medical literature can reveal emerging drug interactions faster than manual review.
exampleCn: 对医学文献的文本挖掘可以比人工审查更快地揭示新兴的药物相互作用。
synonyms: text analytics, knowledge discovery from text
confusableWords: text mining vs. NLP: text mining is the application; NLP provides the techniques. Text mining is more goal-oriented

meaningEn: a learned vector representation of a word that captures semantic and syntactic properties
exampleEn: Word embeddings like Word2Vec and GloVe map words to dense vectors in a continuous space.
exampleCn: Word2Vec和GloVe等词嵌入将单词映射到连续空间中的密集向量。
confusableWords: word embedding vs. contextual embedding: word embedding is static (one vector per word); contextual embedding (e.g., BERT) varies by context

meaningEn: a fixed-size vector representation of an entire sentence, capturing its overall meaning
exampleEn: Sentence embeddings enable semantic search by comparing the similarity of sentence vectors.
exampleCn: 句子嵌入通过比较句子向量的相似性实现语义搜索。
confusableWords: sentence embedding vs. word embedding: sentence embedding represents whole sentences; word embedding represents individual words

meaningEn: an open-source deep learning framework developed by Meta, known for its dynamic computation graphs and Pythonic API
exampleEn: PyTorch has become the dominant framework for academic deep learning research.
exampleCn: PyTorch已成为学术深度学习研究的主导框架。
rootAffix: Py (Python) + Torch (framework name from Torch7 in Lua)
confusableWords: PyTorch vs. TensorFlow: PyTorch is dynamic graph (easier debugging); TensorFlow was static graph (better for production, now supports eager mode too)

meaningEn: an open-source machine learning framework developed by Google, supporting both research and production deployment
exampleEn: TensorFlow provides a complete ecosystem for building and deploying ML models at scale.
exampleCn: TensorFlow提供了大规模构建和部署ML模型的完整生态系统。
confusableWords: TensorFlow vs. Keras: Keras is a high-level API; TensorFlow is the underlying framework. Keras is now integrated into TF

meaningEn: Graphics Processing Unit, a parallel processor originally designed for graphics but widely used for accelerating deep learning computations
exampleEn: Training large language models requires thousands of GPUs running for weeks.
exampleCn: 训练大语言模型需要数千个GPU运行数周。
confusableWords: GPU vs. TPU: GPU is general-purpose parallel processor; TPU is Google's custom ASIC optimized for tensor operations

meaningEn: Tensor Processing Unit, Google's custom ASIC designed specifically to accelerate machine learning workloads
exampleEn: TPUs provide massive matrix multiplication throughput for training very large models efficiently.
exampleCn: TPU为高效训练超大模型提供了大规模矩阵乘法吞吐量。
confusableWords: TPU vs. GPU: TPU is specialized for ML (higher FLOPS/watt for tensors); GPU is general-purpose parallel computing

meaningEn: training a model across multiple compute devices or machines to handle large models or datasets
exampleEn: Distributed training across 256 GPUs reduced the training time from months to days.
exampleCn: 在256个GPU上的分布式训练将训练时间从数月缩短到数天。
confusableWords: distributed training vs. data parallelism: distributed training is the general approach; data parallelism is one specific strategy within it

meaningEn: a distributed training strategy where the dataset is split across devices, each computing gradients on its own data slice
exampleEn: Data parallelism synchronizes gradients across workers using an all-reduce operation.
exampleCn: 数据并行通过all-reduce操作在工作节点之间同步梯度。
confusableWords: data parallelism vs. model parallelism: data parallelism replicates the model; model parallelism splits the model across devices

meaningEn: a distributed training strategy where different parts of a model are placed on different devices
exampleEn: Model parallelism is essential when a model is too large to fit on a single GPU.
exampleCn: 当模型太大无法放入单个GPU时，模型并行是必要的。
confusableWords: pipeline parallelism vs. tensor parallelism: both are types of model parallelism; pipeline splits by layers; tensor splits within layers

meaningEn: a training technique that uses lower-precision (e.g., FP16) alongside higher-precision (FP32) computation to speed up training
exampleEn: Mixed precision training doubled the throughput while maintaining model accuracy.
exampleCn: 混合精度训练在保持模型准确率的同时将吞吐量翻倍。
confusableWords: FP16 vs. BF16: FP16 has smaller dynamic range; BF16 (bfloat16) has the same range as FP32 but lower precision

meaningEn: reducing the precision of model weights (e.g., from FP32 to INT8) to decrease model size and speed up inference
exampleEn: INT8 quantization reduces model size by 4x with minimal accuracy loss.
exampleCn: INT8量化在几乎不损失精度的情况下将模型大小减少了4倍。
confusableWords: post-training quantization vs. quantization-aware training: PTQ quantizes after training; QAT simulates quantization during training for better results

meaningEn: removing less important weights or neurons from a trained model to reduce its size and computational cost
exampleEn: Pruning removed 50% of the model weights while preserving 98% of the original accuracy.
exampleCn: 剪枝移除了50%的模型权重，同时保留了原始准确率的98%。
rootAffix: prune (from Old French proignier, to cut back)
confusableWords: unstructured vs. structured pruning: unstructured removes individual weights; structured removes entire channels/neurons

meaningEn: training a smaller student model to mimic the outputs of a larger teacher model
exampleEn: Knowledge distillation compressed the large teacher model into a mobile-friendly student model.
exampleCn: 知识蒸馏将大型教师模型压缩为适合移动端的学生模型。
confusableWords: knowledge distillation vs. quantization: distillation trains a smaller model; quantization reduces precision of the same model

meaningEn: Open Neural Network Exchange, an open format for representing trained machine learning models portably across frameworks
exampleEn: Exporting the PyTorch model to ONNX format enables deployment in production environments using different runtimes.
exampleCn: 将PyTorch模型导出为ONNX格式使得在不同运行时的生产环境中部署成为可能。
confusableWords: ONNX vs. TensorRT: ONNX is a model format; TensorRT is NVIDIA's inference engine that can optimize ONNX models

meaningEn: NVIDIA's high-performance inference optimizer and runtime for deep learning models
exampleEn: TensorRT optimized the model for deployment, reducing inference latency by 3x.
exampleCn: TensorRT优化了模型用于部署，将推理延迟降低了3倍。
confusableWords: TensorRT vs. ONNX Runtime: TensorRT is NVIDIA-specific (GPU); ONNX Runtime is cross-platform and cross-hardware

meaningEn: the process of making a trained model available for use in a production environment
exampleEn: Model deployment involves containerization, load balancing, and monitoring for drift.
exampleCn: 模型部署涉及容器化、负载均衡和漂移监控。
confusableWords: deployment vs. serving: deployment is the overall process; serving is the runtime inference component

meaningEn: the runtime infrastructure that accepts prediction requests and returns model outputs
exampleEn: TensorFlow Serving provides a flexible, high-performance serving system for ML models.
exampleCn: TensorFlow Serving为ML模型提供了灵活的高性能服务系统。
confusableWords: serving vs. deployment: serving is the inference endpoint; deployment encompasses the entire process of putting a model into production

meaningEn: the time delay between sending a request to a model and receiving the response
exampleEn: Reducing inference latency below 100ms is critical for real-time user-facing applications.
exampleCn: 将推理延迟降低到100ms以下对于面向用户的实时应用至关重要。
confusableWords: latency vs. throughput: latency measures speed per request; throughput measures requests per unit time

meaningEn: the number of inference requests a system can process per unit of time
exampleEn: The inference server achieves a throughput of 1000 requests per second with batch processing.
exampleCn: 推理服务器通过批处理实现了每秒1000个请求的吞吐量。
confusableWords: throughput vs. latency: throughput = how many; latency = how fast. Improving one often affects the other

meaningEn: a saved snapshot of a model's parameters at a specific point during training
exampleEn: Saving model checkpoints every epoch allows resuming training after interruption.
exampleCn: 每个epoch保存模型检查点允许在中断后恢复训练。
confusableWords: checkpoint vs. final model: checkpoints are intermediate saves; the final model is the last checkpoint (or best performing one)

meaningEn: the practice of recording and organizing parameters, metrics, and artifacts from ML experiments
exampleEn: Tools like MLflow and Weights & Biases provide experiment tracking for reproducible ML research.
exampleCn: MLflow和Weights & Biases等工具提供实验追踪以实现可复现的ML研究。
confusableWords: experiment tracking vs. version control: tracking records ML experiments; version control (git) manages code changes

meaningEn: the practice of deploying and maintaining ML models in production reliably and efficiently, combining ML with DevOps
exampleEn: MLOps automates the retraining pipeline when model performance degrades in production.
exampleCn: 当模型在生产中性能下降时，MLOps自动化重新训练流水线。
confusableWords: MLOps vs. DevOps: MLOps extends DevOps principles to ML lifecycle, including data and model management

meaningEn: a sequence of automated steps in an ML workflow, from data processing to model training and deployment
exampleEn: The ML pipeline automates data ingestion, feature engineering, training, and deployment.
exampleCn: ML流水线自动化了数据摄入、特征工程、训练和部署。
confusableWords: pipeline vs. pipeline parallelism: pipeline is an ML workflow concept; pipeline parallelism is a model partitioning strategy

meaningEn: Application Programming Interface, a set of protocols for building and integrating software applications
exampleEn: The model is exposed via a REST API that accepts JSON input and returns predictions.
exampleCn: 模型通过REST API对外暴露，接受JSON输入并返回预测结果。
confusableWords: REST API vs. gRPC: REST uses HTTP/JSON; gRPC uses Protocol Buffers and HTTP/2 for higher performance

meaningEn: a specific URL or address where a deployed model accepts prediction requests
exampleEn: The model endpoint was auto-scaled to handle traffic spikes during peak hours.
exampleCn: 模型端点在高峰时段自动扩容以应对流量激增。
confusableWords: endpoint vs. API: an endpoint is a specific URL; an API is the broader interface specification

meaningEn: a platform for packaging applications and their dependencies into portable containers
exampleEn: Docker containers ensure the model runs consistently across development, staging, and production environments.
exampleCn: Docker容器确保模型在开发、预发布和生产环境中一致运行。
confusableWords: Docker vs. Kubernetes: Docker runs individual containers; Kubernetes orchestrates containers across clusters

meaningEn: an open-source container orchestration platform for automating deployment, scaling, and management of containerized applications
exampleEn: Kubernetes automatically scales model serving pods based on incoming request volume.
exampleCn: Kubernetes根据传入请求量自动扩展模型服务Pod。
confusableWords: Kubernetes vs. Docker Swarm: both orchestrate containers; K8s is more feature-rich and widely adopted; Swarm is simpler

meaningEn: the delivery of computing resources (servers, storage, databases) over the internet on demand
exampleEn: Cloud computing platforms like AWS, GCP, and Azure provide GPU instances for ML training.
exampleCn: AWS、GCP和Azure等云计算平台提供GPU实例用于ML训练。
confusableWords: cloud computing vs. edge computing: cloud is centralized remote servers; edge computing processes data closer to where it's generated

meaningEn: processing data near the source of data generation rather than in a centralized cloud
exampleEn: Edge computing enables real-time inference on mobile devices without sending data to the cloud.
exampleCn: 边缘计算使移动设备能够在不将数据发送到云端的情况下进行实时推理。
confusableWords: edge computing vs. cloud computing: edge processes locally (low latency, privacy); cloud processes remotely (high compute, storage)

meaningEn: a distributed learning approach where models are trained across decentralized devices without sharing raw data
exampleEn: Federated learning allows training on sensitive medical data without moving it to a central server.
exampleCn: 联邦学习允许在不将敏感医疗数据移动到中央服务器的情况下进行训练。
confusableWords: federated learning vs. distributed training: federated learning preserves data privacy; distributed training shares data across nodes

meaningEn: techniques for creating additional training examples by applying transformations to existing data
exampleEn: Data augmentation techniques like random cropping and flipping increased dataset diversity effectively.
exampleCn: 随机裁剪和翻转等数据增强技术有效地增加了数据集的多样性。
confusableWords: data augmentation vs. synthetic data: augmentation transforms real data; synthetic data generates entirely new examples

meaningEn: the steps applied to raw data to clean, normalize, and transform it before feeding it to a model
exampleEn: Text preprocessing includes tokenization, lowercasing, and removing stop words.
exampleCn: 文本预处理包括分词、小写化和去除停用词。
confusableWords: preprocessing vs. feature engineering: preprocessing cleans/normalizes data; feature engineering creates new input variables

meaningEn: the process of creating new input features from raw data to improve model performance
exampleEn: Feature engineering transformed the raw timestamp into day-of-week, hour, and is-weekend features.
exampleCn: 特征工程将原始时间戳转换为了星期几、小时和是否为周末的特征。
confusableWords: feature engineering vs. feature extraction: engineering manually creates features; extraction uses algorithms to learn features automatically

meaningEn: An open-source latent diffusion model capable of generating detailed images from text descriptions
meaningCn: n. 稳定扩散；一种开源的潜在扩散模型，能根据文本描述生成精细图像
exampleEn: Stable diffusion allows users to run text-to-image generation on consumer-grade GPUs.
exampleCn: 稳定扩散允许用户在消费级GPU上运行文本到图像生成。
confusableWords: stable diffusion vs DALL-E: 稳定扩散开源可本地部署，DALL-E为OpenAI闭源API服务

meaningEn: An AI system by OpenAI that generates images from natural language descriptions
meaningCn: n. DALL-E；OpenAI开发的能根据自然语言描述生成图像的AI系统
exampleEn: DALL-E 3 can generate images with remarkably accurate text rendering capabilities.
exampleCn: DALL-E 3能够以极高的准确度在图像中渲染文字。
rootAffix: 命名源自Dali (达利) + WALL-E (机器人瓦力)
confusableWords: DALL-E vs Midjourney: DALL-E由OpenAI开发，文字理解强；Midjourney偏艺术风格，需通过Discord使用

meaningEn: An AI art generator that creates images from textual descriptions, known for its artistic and painterly style
meaningCn: n. Midjourney；一种AI艺术生成器，以艺术性和绘画风格闻名
exampleEn: Midjourney v6 produces highly detailed and aesthetically pleasing artistic images.
exampleCn: Midjourney v6生成高度精细且具有美感的艺术图像。
confusableWords: Midjourney vs Stable Diffusion: Midjourney为闭源SaaS，通过Discord使用；Stable Diffusion开源可本地部署

meaningEn: A type of generative AI model that converts natural language text descriptions into corresponding images
meaningCn: n. 文本到图像；一种将自然语言文本描述转换为对应图像的生成式AI模型
exampleEn: Text-to-image models like DALL-E can illustrate complex concepts described in plain language.
exampleCn: 像DALL-E这样的文本到图像模型能将用通俗语言描述的复杂概念可视化。
confusableWords: text-to-image vs image-to-image: 前者从文字生成图像，后者以图像为输入进行变换或风格迁移

meaningEn: The process of extending an image beyond its original borders by generating new content
meaningCn: n. 图像外延；通过生成新内容将图像扩展到原始边界之外的过程
exampleEn: Outpainting allows artists to expand the canvas of existing images with AI-generated surroundings.
exampleCn: 图像外延使艺术家能够用AI生成的周围环境扩展现有图像的画布。
confusableWords: outpainting vs inpainting: outpainting向外扩展图像，inpainting向内填充图像缺失区域

meaningEn: A compressed representation of data in a lower-dimensional space learned by a neural network
meaningCn: n. 潜在空间；神经网络学习到的数据在低维空间中的压缩表示
exampleEn: Navigating the latent space of a GAN allows smooth interpolation between different generated faces.
exampleCn: 在GAN的潜在空间中导航可以在不同生成面孔之间实现平滑插值。
synonyms: hidden space, embedding space, feature space
confusableWords: latent space vs embedding space: 两者常互换使用，latent space更侧重生成模型，embedding space更侧重表示学习

meaningEn: A predefined plan that controls how much noise is added at each step during the forward diffusion process
meaningCn: n. 噪声调度；控制前向扩散过程中每步添加多少噪声的预设方案
exampleEn: Choosing an appropriate noise schedule is crucial for the quality of diffusion model outputs.
exampleCn: 选择合适的噪声调度对扩散模型输出质量至关重要。
synonyms: noise schedule, variance schedule, beta schedule
confusableWords: noise schedule vs learning rate schedule: 前者控制扩散模型的噪声添加量，后者控制模型训练的学习率变化

meaningEn: The process of removing noise from data, especially in diffusion models where the model learns to reverse noise addition
meaningCn: n. 去噪；从数据中去除噪声的过程，在扩散模型中特指模型学习逆转噪声添加
exampleEn: The denoising process in diffusion models iteratively refines noisy images into clean outputs.
exampleCn: 扩散模型中的去噪过程迭代地将噪声图像精炼为干净输出。
rootAffix: de- (去除) + noise (噪声) + -ing (动名词后缀)
confusableWords: denoising vs noise reduction: 两者含义相近，denoising在深度学习语境中更常用，尤指扩散模型

meaningEn: A generative model that estimates the gradient (score) of the log probability density and uses it for sampling
meaningCn: n. 基于分数的模型；一种估计对数概率密度梯度（分数）并用于采样的生成模型
exampleEn: Score-based models provide a unified framework for both diffusion and Langevin dynamics sampling.
exampleCn: 基于分数的模型为扩散和朗之万动力学采样提供了统一框架。
rootAffix: score (分数/得分) + based (基于) + model
synonyms: score matching model, score generative model
confusableWords: score-based model vs diffusion model: 基于分数的模型是更一般化的理论框架，扩散模型是其特例

meaningEn: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model; a foundational diffusion model that uses a Markov chain of noise addition and removal
meaningCn: n. 去噪扩散概率模型；一种基础扩散模型，使用噪声添加和去除的马尔可夫链
exampleEn: DDPM demonstrated that iterative denoising can produce high-quality generative samples.
exampleCn: DDPM证明了迭代去噪可以产生高质量的生成样本。
rootAffix: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model 缩写
confusableWords: DDPM vs DDIM: DDPM为概率模型，采样需多步；DDIM为隐式模型，可用更少步数生成

meaningEn: Latent Diffusion Model; a diffusion model that operates in a compressed latent space rather than pixel space
meaningCn: n. 潜在扩散模型；在压缩的潜在空间而非像素空间中操作的扩散模型
exampleEn: Stable diffusion is based on LDM, which dramatically reduces computational cost compared to pixel-space diffusion.
exampleCn: 稳定扩散基于LDM，与像素空间扩散相比大幅降低了计算成本。
confusableWords: LDM vs DDPM: LDM在潜在空间操作效率更高，DDPM直接在像素空间操作计算量大

meaningEn: A neural network architecture that adds spatial conditioning to diffusion models for controlled image generation
meaningCn: n. 控制网络；一种向扩散模型添加空间条件以实现可控图像生成的神经网络架构
exampleEn: Control net enables users to guide image generation using edge maps, depth maps, or pose skeletons.
exampleCn: 控制网络使用户能够使用边缘图、深度图或姿态骨架来引导图像生成。
confusableWords: control net vs prompt conditioning: 前者提供空间级控制（如轮廓、深度），后者通过文字描述控制

meaningEn: A generative AI model that creates video content from text descriptions
meaningCn: n. 文本到视频；从文本描述生成视频内容的生成式AI模型
exampleEn: Sora is a text-to-video model capable of generating minute-long videos with complex scenes.
exampleCn: Sora是一种文本到视频模型，能生成长达一分钟、包含复杂场景的视频。
confusableWords: text-to-video vs text-to-image: 前者生成时序连贯的视频帧序列，后者生成单张静态图像

meaningEn: The use of AI models to create new video content, either from text prompts or other conditioning inputs
meaningCn: n. 视频生成；使用AI模型创建新视频内容，可基于文本提示或其他条件输入
exampleEn: Video generation models must maintain temporal consistency across frames to produce coherent motion.
exampleCn: 视频生成模型必须跨帧保持时间一致性以产生连贯的运动。
confusableWords: video generation vs video prediction: 生成创建全新视频，预测根据已有帧推测未来帧

meaningEn: The process of recording the movement of objects or people using sensors or cameras for animation or analysis
meaningCn: n. 动作捕捉；使用传感器或相机记录物体或人运动用于动画或分析的过程
exampleEn: Motion capture technology is essential for creating realistic character animations in video games.
exampleCn: 动作捕捉技术对在电子游戏中创建逼真的角色动画至关重要。
confusableWords: motion capture vs pose estimation: 动作捕捉用专用传感器精度更高，姿态估计用普通相机精度较低

meaningEn: The interpretation of human gestures using mathematical algorithms, typically for human-computer interaction
meaningCn: n. 手势识别；使用数学算法解释人类手势，通常用于人机交互
exampleEn: Gesture recognition enables touchless control of smart devices through hand movements.
exampleCn: 手势识别使通过手部动作无触摸控制智能设备成为可能。
confusableWords: gesture recognition vs pose estimation: 手势识别关注手部动作的含义，姿态估计关注全身关节位置

meaningEn: The use of AI to identify human emotional states from facial expressions, voice, or text
meaningCn: n. 情绪检测；使用AI从面部表情、语音或文本识别人类情绪状态
exampleEn: Emotion detection systems analyze facial micro-expressions to assess customer satisfaction in real time.
exampleCn: 情绪检测系统通过分析面部微表情来实时评估客户满意度。
confusableWords: emotion detection vs sentiment analysis: 前者通常指视觉/语音模态，后者通常指文本模态

meaningEn: The use of AI and computational techniques to analyze and interpret medical images such as X-rays, MRIs, and CT scans
meaningCn: n. 医学影像；使用AI和计算技术分析和解释X光、MRI和CT扫描等医学图像
exampleEn: Deep learning has significantly improved the accuracy of tumor detection in medical imaging.
exampleCn: 深度学习显著提高了医学影像中肿瘤检测的准确性。
confusableWords: medical imaging vs computer vision: 前者专指医疗领域，后者是涵盖范围更广的通用视觉任务

meaningEn: A model-free reinforcement learning algorithm that learns the value of actions in each state without requiring a model of the environment
meaningCn: n. Q学习；一种无模型强化学习算法，学习每个状态下动作的价值而不需要环境模型
exampleEn: Q-learning converges to the optimal policy as long as all state-action pairs are visited sufficiently often.
exampleCn: 只要所有状态-动作对被充分访问，Q学习就会收敛到最优策略。
rootAffix: Q (quality/value 质量/价值) + learning (学习)
confusableWords: Q-learning vs SARSA: Q-learning是off-policy算法，SARSA是on-policy算法

meaningEn: A family of reinforcement learning algorithms that optimize the policy directly by computing gradients of the expected reward
meaningCn: n. 策略梯度；一种直接通过计算期望奖励的梯度来优化策略的强化学习算法族
exampleEn: Policy gradient methods can handle continuous action spaces that Q-learning struggles with.
exampleCn: 策略梯度方法可以处理Q学习难以应对的连续动作空间。
confusableWords: policy gradient vs Q-learning: 策略梯度直接优化策略函数，Q-learning间接通过价值函数选动作

meaningEn: A reinforcement learning architecture that combines a policy network (actor) with a value network (critic) for more stable training
meaningCn: n. 演员-评论家；一种结合策略网络（演员）和价值网络（评论家）以实现更稳定训练的强化学习架构
exampleEn: Actor-critic methods like A3C and PPO achieve better sample efficiency than pure policy gradient approaches.
exampleCn: A3C和PPO等演员-评论家方法比纯策略梯度方法具有更好的样本效率。
rootAffix: actor (演员/执行者) + critic (评论家/评判者)
confusableWords: actor-critic vs REINFORCE: actor-critic引入评论家网络降低方差，REINFORCE只有演员网络方差大

meaningEn: A method in reinforcement learning that estimates value by averaging returns from complete episodes using random sampling
meaningCn: n. 蒙特卡洛；一种强化学习方法，通过随机采样完整回合的回报平均值来估计价值
exampleEn: Monte Carlo methods require complete episodes before updating value estimates, unlike temporal difference methods.
exampleCn: 蒙特卡洛方法需要完整回合才能更新价值估计，这与时序差分方法不同。
rootAffix: 得名于Monte Carlo赌场（摩纳哥），代表随机/概率
confusableWords: Monte Carlo vs temporal difference: MC需要完整回合更新，TD可以逐步在线更新

meaningEn: A class of reinforcement learning methods that combine Monte Carlo sampling with dynamic programming by updating estimates based on other estimates
meaningCn: n. 时序差分；一种结合蒙特卡洛采样和动态规划的强化学习方法，基于其他估计值更新估计
exampleEn: Temporal difference learning is the foundation of many modern reinforcement learning algorithms including Q-learning.
exampleCn: 时序差分学习是包括Q学习在内的许多现代强化学习算法的基础。
confusableWords: TD(0) vs TD(λ): TD(0)只使用一步回报，TD(λ)使用多步回报的加权组合

meaningEn: In reinforcement learning, the strategy of trying new actions to discover potentially better rewards in unexplored states
meaningCn: n. 探索；在强化学习中，尝试新动作以发现未探索状态中潜在更好奖励的策略
exampleEn: Balancing exploration and exploitation is one of the fundamental challenges in reinforcement learning.
exampleCn: 平衡探索与利用是强化学习的根本挑战之一。
rootAffix: ex- (向外) + plorare (探究) + -ation (名词后缀)
confusableWords: exploration vs exploitation: 探索尝试新策略寻找最优，利用坚持已知最优策略

meaningEn: In reinforcement learning, the strategy of choosing actions that have previously yielded the highest rewards
meaningCn: n. 利用；在强化学习中，选择先前产生最高奖励的动作的策略
exampleEn: An agent that only uses exploitation may get stuck in a suboptimal policy by never trying alternatives.
exampleCn: 只使用利用策略的智能体可能因从不尝试替代方案而陷入次优策略。
confusableWords: exploitation (RL) vs exploitation (伦理): RL中指利用已有知识，日常用语中指剥削

meaningEn: A scalar feedback signal given to a reinforcement learning agent after each action to indicate how good the action was
meaningCn: n. 奖励；强化学习中每次动作后给予智能体的标量反馈信号，表示动作的好坏程度
exampleEn: Designing an effective reward function is often the most difficult part of applying reinforcement learning.
exampleCn: 设计有效的奖励函数通常是应用强化学习最困难的部分。
rootAffix: re- (再次) + ward (看守/守护) → 守护回报
confusableWords: reward vs return: reward是单步反馈，return是累积折扣奖励

meaningEn: A value between 0 and 1 that determines the present value of future rewards in reinforcement learning
meaningCn: n. 折扣因子；一个0到1之间的值，决定强化学习中未来奖励的现值
exampleEn: A discount factor close to 1 makes the agent value long-term rewards, while a value near 0 makes it myopic.
exampleCn: 接近1的折扣因子使智能体重视长期奖励，接近0则使其目光短浅。
confusableWords: discount factor vs learning rate: 前者控制未来奖励的权重，后者控制参数更新的步长

meaningEn: A function that estimates the expected cumulative reward a reinforcement learning agent can obtain from a given state
meaningCn: n. 价值函数；估计强化学习智能体从给定状态可获得期望累积奖励的函数
exampleEn: The value function guides the agent toward states with higher long-term expected returns.
exampleCn: 价值函数引导智能体趋向具有更高长期期望回报的状态。
confusableWords: value function vs Q-function: 价值函数V(s)评估状态价值，Q函数Q(s,a)评估状态-动作价值

meaningEn: A function that estimates the expected cumulative reward of taking a specific action in a specific state
meaningCn: n. Q函数；估计在特定状态执行特定动作的期望累积奖励的函数
exampleEn: The optimal Q-function allows the agent to select the best action for any given state.
exampleCn: 最优Q函数使智能体能对任何给定状态选择最佳动作。
confusableWords: Q-function vs value function: Q-function同时考虑状态和动作，value function只考虑状态

meaningEn: In reinforcement learning, the current situation or configuration of the environment that the agent observes
meaningCn: n. 状态；在强化学习中，智能体观察到的环境的当前情况或配置
exampleEn: The state representation must contain all relevant information the agent needs to make optimal decisions.
exampleCn: 状态表示必须包含智能体做出最优决策所需的全部相关信息。
confusableWords: state vs observation: 理想中state包含所有信息（POMDP中observation是state的部分观测）

meaningEn: In reinforcement learning, a decision or move made by the agent that affects the environment and transitions it to a new state
meaningCn: n. 动作；在强化学习中，智能体做出的影响环境并将其转换到新状态的决策或行动
exampleEn: The action space defines the set of all possible moves available to the reinforcement learning agent.
exampleCn: 动作空间定义了强化学习智能体可用的所有可能行动集合。
confusableWords: action space vs state space: 前者定义可选动作集合，后者定义环境可能的配置集合

meaningEn: In reinforcement learning, everything external to the agent that it interacts with, which responds to actions and provides observations and rewards
meaningCn: n. 环境；在强化学习中，智能体与之交互的所有外部事物，响应动作并提供观察和奖励
exampleEn: The OpenAI Gym toolkit provides standardized environments for benchmarking reinforcement learning algorithms.
exampleCn: OpenAI Gym工具包提供了用于基准测试强化学习算法的标准化环境。
rootAffix: en- (在...内) + viron (围绕) + -ment (名词后缀)
confusableWords: environment (RL) vs environment (软件): RL中是智能体的交互世界，软件中指运行配置

meaningEn: In reinforcement learning, an entity that perceives its environment, takes actions, and learns from the resulting rewards
meaningCn: n. 智能体；在强化学习中，感知环境、执行动作并从结果奖励中学习的实体
exampleEn: The reinforcement learning agent iteratively improves its policy through interaction with the environment.
exampleCn: 强化学习智能体通过与环境的交互迭代改进其策略。
confusableWords: agent (RL) vs agent (软件): RL agent是学习决策者，software agent是自动执行任务的程序

meaningEn: Markov Decision Process; a mathematical framework for modeling sequential decision-making where outcomes are partly random and partly under control
meaningCn: n. 马尔可夫决策过程；一种建模序列决策的数学框架，结果部分随机部分可控
exampleEn: Most reinforcement learning problems are formulated as MDPs to provide a rigorous theoretical foundation.
exampleCn: 大多数强化学习问题被构建为MDP以提供严谨的理论基础。
confusableWords: MDP vs POMDP: MDP假设完全可观测状态，POMDP处理部分可观测状态

meaningEn: A mathematical framework for decision-making in situations where outcomes are probabilistic and the future depends only on the current state
meaningCn: n. 马尔可夫决策过程；一种在结果具有概率性且未来仅取决于当前状态的情境下进行决策的数学框架
exampleEn: The Markov property ensures that the future is independent of the past given the present state.
exampleCn: 马尔可夫性质确保在给定当前状态的条件下，未来与过去相互独立。
rootAffix: Markov (人名Andrey Markov) + decision (决策) + process (过程)
